proposals.relationship: Owram credits reading The Sense of Power with leading him to seek doctoral study under Berger, whose supervision helped develop his historical work.
proposals.evidence_note: Joint Owram/Friesen introduction3–4 gives Owram’s particular choice, distinguishes Friesen’s inherited supervision after Cook left, and describes perceptive comments while insisting students’ work remain their own. Recipient-authored account, beyond affiliation alone; no claim every festschrift contributor was a student or that Owram adopted every interpretation. 1970 first book and2011 testimony distinct; 2013 edition introduction not substituted.

primary_locators.passage: Owram reading and application; intellectual supervision with independence.

proposals.relationship: Cook identifies Innis’s concern for limitations and tentativeness as a methodological example that Berger approved and implicitly recommended.
proposals.evidence_note: Cook2011p13 explicitly interprets Berger’s account of Innis this way and n1 cites The Writing of Canadian History1976p107. This is attributed substantive scholarly mediation of a particular methodological resource, not direct formation testimony or inference from Innis being a book subject. Cook15 also records Berger’s reservations about Innis’s nationalist instruction; positive resource coexists with criticism. Berger original107 unread.

primary_locators.passage: Approved concern for limitations and tentativeness; not blanket endorsement.

proposals.relationship: Cook describes Berger’s reservations when Innis departed from historical detachment to teach nationalist lessons.
proposals.evidence_note: Cook2011p15 specifically says even Innis’s nationalist pulpit made Berger uneasy, n8 cites1976book chapter4 and190–191. Critique attributed to Cook’s substantive account, limited to nationalist present-minded instruction, alongside Berger’s admiration for Innis’s tentativeness. No assertion all Innis economics or communications work rejected; original cited pages unread.

primary_locators.passage: Unease at nationalist lessons despite admiration for detachment.

proposals.relationship: Gauvreau reads The Sense of Power as reasserting Careless’s pattern of ideological conflict followed by national consensus.
proposals.evidence_note: Gauvreau2011p60 explicitly compares Berger’s narrative with the Careless master narrative, while acknowledging Berger’s innovative disaggregation of conservative nationalism at59. An attributed undirected comparison of historiographical structures; doctoral supervision independently documented in repository finding aid, but does not convert this analytical comparison into proven personal transmission. No claim every Careless framework shared or directly adopted.

primary_locators.passage: Careless supervision is separate role evidence.

proposals.relationship: Cook questions Berger’s claim that the Darwinian controversy was not a conflict between religion and science.
proposals.evidence_note: Cook2011p22 grants participants crossed clerical/scientific categories but calls that insufficient, arguing Berger’s own distinction between retaining theology and excluding creation/providence amounts to natural theology versus scientific naturalism. Precise objection to Science, God and Nature1983pp54–55, not dismissal of book: Cook22–23 praises original findings and contextual method. Note31 identifies James R. Moore’s1979 argument as Berger’s simplified source; Moore original unread and missing endpoint.

primary_locators.passage: Literal role classification insufficient; theology/naturalism distinction; praise retained.

proposals.relationship: Gauvreau presents Berger’s Canadian-nationalist interpretation of imperialism as a revision of the externally imposed, alien imperialism account earlier restated by Cook.
proposals.evidence_note: Gauvreau2011p59 explicitly names Underhill and Cook’s early1960s position, then explains Berger’s reversal as locally produced nationalism. Attributed scholarly reconstruction of a specific interpretive disagreement; not claim Berger personally denounced Cook or that Cook never revised his view. Cook2011 warmly endorses the thesis, so later agreement is retained. Underhill missing endpoint and distinct role. Original early Cook account and Berger complete book unread.

primary_locators.passage: Named earlier Cook/Underhill model and Berger’s interpretive reversal.
Later Cook endorsement coexists with earlier difference.
